intro: Begun after a trip to Mardi Gras in New Orleans in February 1964 and finished that spring. Dylan sang it for a year before releasing it — by which time the Byrds were about to turn it into a number one.

lives.title: First performance
lives.note: Probably the live debut, months before any recording was released.

lives.title: With Ramblin' Jack Elliott
lives.note: Tried during the Another Side sessions with Elliott singing harmony. Left off the album, it surfaced in 2005 on No Direction Home.

lives.title: Newport 1964
lives.note: Sung solo at the festival a year before the electric set; the crowd was hearing it for the first time.

lives.title: The master take
lives.note: Acoustic guitar and harmonica with Bruce Langhorne's electric guitar weaving around them. On Bringing It All Back Home, March 1965.

lives.title: The Byrds
lives.note: One of his four verses, a jangling twelve-string guitar and close harmonies. Number one in the US and UK, and often called the start of folk rock.

lives.title: End of the acoustic half
lives.note: On the 1966 world tour it closed the solo acoustic set every night, stretched out with long harmonica passages. On The Bootleg Series Vol. 4.

lives.title: With flute
lives.note: The 1978 band gave it a gentle arrangement with flute. On Bob Dylan at Budokan.

others.note: Number one on both sides of the Atlantic.
An early folk cover on her Fifth Album.
